title: Draupadi's question
hook: Bhima answers with fire, Arjuna holds him back, and Vikarna, a Kaurava, answers with reasons

segments.voice: Yesterday Bhishma said the ways of dharma are subtle, and left Draupadi's question unsettled while she stood waiting.

Two voices break the silence, and they break it in opposite directions. First Bhima. He has watched his eldest brother stake him, lose him, and then lose Draupadi, and his anger has nowhere to go. In the telling, he turns it on Yudhishthira himself. Then someone nobody expects speaks up, a young man from the other side of the family. Two answers to Draupadi's question: one made of fury, one made of reasons.
screen: `TWO VOICES BREAK THE SILENCE.` → `ONE WITH FURY.` → `ONE WITH REASONS.`

segments.voice: Bhima's words are shocking. Gamblers, he says, don't stake even the women kept in their houses. Then he turns to Sahadeva: bring fire, and I'll burn this brother's arms. It's the rage of someone who loves his brother and can't bear what his brother has done. Arjuna stops him. In effect he says: our enemies want exactly this, to see us turn on our eldest. Yudhishthira was challenged, and he kept a warrior's custom. And Bhima holds back. Then Vikarna speaks. He's one of Duryodhana's own brothers, a Kaurava, and he stands up in his family's hall and says: answer her. Nobody does. So he answers it himself, with reasons. Kings, he says, are prone to certain vices: hunting, drinking, dice, and too much pleasure. A man in the grip of one of them acts without judgment. Yudhishthira staked Draupadi in the grip of the game, and only when Shakuni prompted him. He had already lost himself. And she's the wife of all five brothers, not his alone. For these reasons, Vikarna says, she was not won. The hall erupts. Voices across the hall cheer him and blame Shakuni. For a moment it looks as if the question has an answer. Notice who gave it: not an elder, not a Pandava, but a younger brother of the winning side, willing to say the unwelcome thing to his own family.
screen: `BHIMA: BRING FIRE.` · `ARJUNA: THAT'S WHAT OUR ENEMIES WANT.` · `VIKARNA, A KAURAVA, STANDS UP.` · `HIS REASONS: SHE WAS NOT WON.` · then, large: `THE HALL CHEERS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a time someone on your own side did something wrong, whether you stayed quiet to keep the peace or spoke up, and picture the moment without judging yourself. Let one calm sentence come that you could have said, a reason rather than a shout, and breathe with it. If you pray, you can bring that moment into your prayer; if not, let the quiet hold it.
Draupadi's question. Bhima answers with fire, Arjuna holds him back, and Vikarna, a Kaurava, answers with reasons: she was not won.
Your line: she was not won. Tomorrow, someone answers Vikarna back. Day seven hundred seventy-two, done.

howItsDone: Vikarna is remembered in retellings as the Kaurava who spoke for Draupadi, and Arjuna's restraint of Bhima is told as a moment when the brothers refused to turn on each other.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. Bhima is calling for fire to burn your eldest brother's hands. what do you do?
options: remind him that this is what your enemies want.
fork.reveal: Arjuna says their enemies want them to turn on their eldest, and that Yudhishthira kept a warrior's custom; Bhima holds back.

original.note: Sanskrit vyasana: a vice or ruinous habit; Vikarna names the vices that cloud a king's judgment.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Kauravas were all on one side.
what it means: Vikarna, Duryodhana's own brother, gives reasons Draupadi was not won.
what a scholar hears: Vikarna argues from the king's vices, the order of the stakes and her being wife to all five, a case in law, not just sympathy.
recall: warned the game would bring quarrel

chat.says: Did anyone in that hall actually stand up for Draupadi?
options: Yes. Vikarna, one of Duryodhana's own brothers, gave reasons she was not won.
Yes. Arjuna argued her case, while Bhima stayed quiet the whole time.
No. Not one person in the hall said a single word for her.
chat.meaning: Vikarna, a Kaurava, said Yudhishthira staked her in the grip of the game, after losing himself. She was not won.

Vikarna.meaning: a brother of Duryodhana who speaks up for Draupadi

Kaurava.meaning: a son of Dhritarashtra, on Duryodhana's side of the family

Sahadeva.meaning: the youngest of the five Pandava brothers

Arjuna.meaning: the third Pandava brother, a great archer

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Dyuta Parva (Bhima's anger at Yudhishthira and call for fire; Arjuna's restraint; Vikarna's speech on the four vices of kings, the order of the stakes and Draupadi as wife of all five; the assembly's applause)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm Bhima's words (gamblers do not stake even their serving women; 'Sahadeva, bring fire, I will burn his arms/hands').
Confirm Arjuna's reply: their enemies want them to violate their duty to the eldest; Yudhishthira was summoned and played according to kshatriya usage.

Confirm Vikarna's four vices (hunting, drinking, dice, excessive attachment to women), and his points: staked while addicted, at Shakuni's prompting, after losing himself, and she is the common wife of the five.
'Many of those present cheer him and blame Shakuni' follows the text's description of a loud uproar applauding Vikarna and censuring Shakuni; confirm.
Original: vyasana as the term for these royal vices; confirm.

Editor: hook said 'two brothers' for Bhima and Vikarna, now 'two voices'; fixed garbled word order; Bhima's paraphrase follows Ganguli more closely (women kept in gamblers' houses, arms not hands); 'many of those present' softened.
